messages:
Marcus (Acct Exec): Hey team — Enterprise bank wants a hosted POC next week. Need temporary higher QPS for a live demo (video walkthrough + automated load). Can we do ~250 qps for a 48h window and IP allowlist their demo infra? Also need scoped keys and rotation guidance.
Rohan (Solutions): We can do a temporary hosted quota bump. Two options: quick scoped-key bump on hosted API (fast) or short Dedicated pool (more predictable latency for demo). For 48h we usually do a scoped key + per-key QPS raise.
Lina (SRE): We’ll need the customer IPs/CIDRs for allowlisting. Prefer CIDR ranges over single IPs. Also confirm whether they’ll use NAT egress or ephemeral cloud runners.
Marcus (Acct Exec): They run the demo from a partner VM + Zoom host (two IPs). I'll get the IP list today. Any TTL limit on scoped keys? Security wants auto-expiry.
Rohan (Solutions): Scoped keys support TTLs. Recommend: create a scoped key with 2h TTL for the demo sessions, rotate between runs. For the overall 48h window we can provision a long-lived scoped admin key for ops and several short-lived keys for demos. Example create call via our internal key manager API:

```
# create scoped key (example)
POST /internal/keys
{
  "parent_key": "sk-live-xxx",
  "scopes": ["completion:write","model:use"],
  "qps": 250,
  "ttl_seconds": 7200,
  "allowed_cidrs": ["203.0.113.8/32","198.51.100.4/32"]
}
```

Rohan (Solutions): That will return a scoped_key token and metadata. We'll also attach rate-limit tags for monitoring and a temporary quota bucket (so we don't touch global limits).
Ava (Sales): If the customer asks about Dedicated — how fast could we spin a small pool? They asked about latency guarantees.
Rohan (Solutions): Dedicated pool requires capacity commit and infra provisioning; for ad-hoc demos we can sometimes allocate a short-lived Dedicated node (subject to capacity) but it's slower (24–48h) and needs a billing commit. Hosted with scoped keys is fastest.
Lina (SRE): For allowlisting: we add the CIDRs to the frontend ACL and tag the scoped key. We'll log requests with the scoped key ID for audit. We need the security questionnaire entry for "token rotation / ephemeral keys" — security-bot can auto-fill once we attach docs.
security-bot: FYI: security FAQ link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/security/poc-keys. I can attach the standard SOC2 section and an example IP-allowlist snippet to the questionnaire.
Marcus (Acct Exec): Perfect. I'll collect the two demo IPs and customer contact. Can you draft a short runbook for the demo provisioning steps + rollback? They want the process documented for compliance.
Rohan (Solutions): Will do. Draft runbook steps: 1) get IPs & schedule; 2) create scoped key w/ QPS=250 & CIDRs; 3) attach to temporary quota bucket; 4) validate with smoke load (10m); 5) monitor latencies & errors; 6) auto-revoke keys at window end. I'll drop the runbook in the channel and ping infra.
Lina (SRE): Add alert: error rate > 1% or p95 latency > 350ms — auto-scale or fallback to lower-QPS model. We'll also capture token-level logs for the audit trail.
Marcus (Acct Exec): Awesome — target provisioning tomorrow 09:00 PT. I'll send IPs by EOD.
Ava (Sales): Noted. I'll loop in legal if they want an amendment for the demo commit.
Marcus (Acct Exec): Thanks! :thumbsup:
Rohan (Solutions): I'll prepare the scoped-key template and test it on staging. Ping me if you want a dry run.
Lina (SRE): Logging and ACL changes queued. I'll approve once Marcus posts IPs.
security-bot: Security questionnaire updated with new scoped-key guidance by @security-bot at 2026-03-21.
Marcus (Acct Exec): Closing loop — IPs sent to infra email and contact is sarah@enterprisebank.com. Proceed when ready.
